_capture.note: Captured from one permission dialog in a throwaway Claude Code session in default permission mode, by temporary command hooks that each wrote their payload to a file named by `date +%s%3N`, then sanitised by a script that refuses to write if any raw string of six or more characters survives outside a named allowlist. Do not hand-edit; re-capture instead. Keys are exactly as captured, in captured order. Kept verbatim: hook_event_name, permission_mode, effort.level, tool_name, notification_type, message. Ids are stable fakes in the captured format, so events that shared an id still share one, including the uuid inside transcript_path and scratchpad_dir. The home directory is /home/user, the repo is /home/user/repo, the profile directory is ~/.claude, and Claude's per-project directory names follow the fake cwd; the uid in /tmp/claude-<uid> is kept. Command text, the call's description and every value inside permission_suggestions are replaced by markers, keeping the list and its keys. afterMs is measured from the first record by the probe's own clock at each hook's start, so it includes a command hook's spawn time; #86's table, from another dialog, has PermissionRequest at +0.41s and the Notification at +6.58s.
settles: PermissionRequest fired before the dialog, seconds before the Notification astir used to block on: here 1.1s after PreToolUse, and the permission_prompt Notification 6.4s after it.
PermissionRequest carries tool_name, tool_input and permission_suggestions, but no tool_use_id and no agent_id. This one is the main agent's, which is named by session_id.
PermissionRequest's tool_input is the PreToolUse's, unchanged.
The Notification names no tool: notification_type permission_prompt and a fixed message.
measuredAlongside: Esc at the dialog fired no hook at all: no PermissionDenied, Stop, StopFailure or PostToolUseFailure.
When auto mode's classifier approved without a dialog, PermissionRequest did not fire: PreToolUse, then PostToolUse.
AskUserQuestion fired PermissionRequest (tool_name AskUserQuestion), then a permission_prompt Notification.

`claude agents --json` reported the session `waiting` while a dialog was open, `idle` after Esc or once the turn had ended, and `busy` while working. For AskUserQuestion it read `busy` at ~1s and `waiting` by ~7s.
measuredSince: On 2.1.312, `claude agents --json` names what a waiting session waits for, as `waitingFor` beside `status: waiting`. Four of thirteen sessions on the machine read `waiting` with `waitingFor: input needed`, one of them while it was working.
readFromTheBinary: PermissionRequest is not the dialog itself. Claude also runs PermissionRequest hooks for an ask that can never show one (shouldAvoidPermissionPrompts: a background agent, a headless session), and then denies the ask itself. Read from 2.1.312, not measured.

`waitingFor` is `permission prompt` for a tool's permission dialog; `input needed` for AskUserQuestion, an MCP elicitation, and an elicitation queued behind another dialog, which outranks everything, work included; and `dialog open`, `worker request`, `sandbox request` or `goal proposal` otherwise. Read from 2.1.296 to 2.1.312.
`claude agents --json` reports every status but `idle` and `waiting` as `busy`, so a session file's `shell` (idle with a background shell running) arrives as `busy`. Read from 2.1.296 to 2.1.312.
The permission_prompt Notification is sent only while the dialog is still up, once the user has been idle at it for 6s, checked every 6s. Read from 2.1.312.
